A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 32-page MTSQL-R1 study, including Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that the scientific material is identical; differences concern the bibliography and first-page version stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoSQL and SParC experiments, including trained-model results in Table 2, tool ablations in Table 4, and additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CoSQL and SParC results, tool ablations, training analyses and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same MDP actions, execution and memory verification, self-taught warm-start SFT, curriculum RL, reward functions and loss masking.

E1.justification: Both versions use CoSQL and SParC with the same in-domain and cross-dataset evaluations, dialogue-turn coverage and SQL difficulty categories.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2–4, including ACT-SQL, CoE-SQL, GAZP+BERT, RASAT+PICARD and the Qwen baselines. Bibliographic revisions do not change the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, model configurations, training budgets and testing procedures are unchanged. Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same EX/EM definitions, model sizes, rollout settings and response limits.

E4.justification: Both retain identical training-stage and tool ablations, difficulty and turn analyses, error analysis, training dynamics, and the execution-correction and memory-verification cases in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including plotted error bars and shaded bands. No seed information, repeated-run disclosures or statistical estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and case-study outcomes are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports the same 77.6% average EX and 66.5% average EM for the 4B model with outcome-plus-process RL.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, action-transition rule in Equation 1, reward mathematics, SFT objective and GRPO formulation are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, training contributions, and claims about performance, coherence and cross-domain generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of verification, self-correction and training dynamics are unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning aggregation drift, extra-hard queries and the latency/accuracy tradeoff discussed in Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: Appendix B's hardware, hyperparameters and tool configurations, and Appendix E's error-classification prompt are identical. The repository link and promise to release models, logs and trajectories after internal review also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and their roles in the argument remain the same. Revised entries for IGSQL, RAT-SQL, PICARD and other retained works concern bibliographic metadata; Section 2 and the research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Several bibliography entries revise or expand author names, titles and publication details, replacing placeholders such as '2021 NLP conference.' The arXiv version/date stamp changes; main-text wording and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded bibliography entries alter line wrapping and placement across pages 11–12, and several titles gain hyperlink styling. All figures, tables, captions and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces vague bibliography placeholders with specific authors, titles, venues and page ranges, and adds links for several retained references. This improves reference traceability and documentation. The methods, empirical evidence and appendices are identical, so the overall quality gain is limited.
